title: Shared definitions of the role output schemas
description: Not an output schema itself: the others refer to its $defs. Every object lists all its properties as required and forbids others, so the schemas also work with runtimes that enforce strict structured output.

criterion_id.description: Acceptance criterion ID from the spec, e.g. AC-3.

assumption.description: Something taken as true without confirmation. Forecrew registers it as A-n (docs/contracts/data-model.md, assumptions); docs/contracts/council-brief.schema.json repeats this definition.

statement.description: What you take as true, as one sentence.

confidence.description: How sure you are the assumption holds.

impact.description: How much the result changes if the assumption is wrong.

verify_by.description: How it can be checked: a test, a question to a human, or research.

assumptions.description: Every assumption you made; an empty list only if you made none.

member.description: A council member: its role and the runtime its jobs run on, as role@runtime (architect@claude-code), as council.read names it. One role may sit on several runtimes, so the role alone does not name a member.

evidence.description: A claim of a council member and the source that backs it. Forecrew checks every source after the contribution: paths and KB paths must exist at the council's commit, URLs are fetched and archived, jobs must exist. An unchecked or missing source weakens the claim in the synthesis.

kind.description: path: a file of the repo; kb: a knowledge entry; url: a public web page; job: an earlier Forecrew job.

source.description: path: relative to the repo root, optionally with :line or :start-end (internal/queue/lease.go:40-58); kb: the entry's path (docs/adr/0003-queue.md); url: an absolute http(s) URL; job: its ref (JOB-12).

date.description: For a url: the date the page was published or, when it shows none, the day you read it, as YYYY-MM-DD. null for other kinds.

confidence.description: How sure you are that the source supports the claim.

escalation.description: Set when you stopped because of an escalation condition: what a human must decide or provide. null otherwise.
